title: feat: upgrade Windows node sandboxing to MXC 1.0 .NET SDK

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Makes Windows-node command containment easier to configure and more reliable, replacing the legacy executable bridge with the official MXC .NET SDK.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Users can choose Strict, Balanced or Open, then edit preset and custom folders using **No access / Read only / Read and write**. Explicitly allowed children remain accessible below a user-denied parent; protected application and credential locations remain non-overridable.

**Intentional security-policy change:** Windows UI API compatibility is always available inside MXC. The default-off toggle and saved legacy restriction are retired. This removes optional Win32k syscall blocking, not command approvals, container desktop isolation, desktop-control/input-injection restrictions, or filesystem/network/clipboard policy.

Supported Windows requires BaseContainer with native protected-path denies and no host ACL augmentation. Only positively identified unsupported Windows permits visibly warned, approved uncontained compatibility execution, where sandbox restrictions are not enforced. Missing SDK components, uncertain probes, policy errors and execution failures block instead of downgrading. Turning off **Run system tools** blocks node `system.run`, not the Gateway's separate `exec` tool.

Maintainer repairs preserve approved multiline direct arguments, reject noncanonical combined/embedded cmd command switches, report eight occupied execution slots as a retryable capacity error rather than a sandbox denial, and protect `.openclaw-companion` cleanup state even under Open.

**Known blocking compatibility failure:** on the tested Windows ARM64 build 26710, renaming a file inside the SDK-created TEMP directory returns Access denied. This can break tools that rename temporary files. Current-head native proof reproduces [microsoft/mxc#1204](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1204); no broad package-directory grant or custom TEMP workaround is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Use `Microsoft.Mxc.Sdk` 1.0.0 directly instead of extracting an npm-supplied executable and maintaining a custom transport. `MxcRequestBuilder` owns the complete SDK request, `MxcCommandRunner` owns process/cancellation/finalization lifetime, and `MxcRequestContext` supplies immutable logical/physical private-state protection. Legacy executors remain deleted.

The migration preserves captured output at deadlines, separates root exit from SDK finalization, admits verified Cloud Files directories, protects registered Store/Dev Companion state, and rejects invalid scratch roots before creating directories. Cleanup removes only the four historically shipped legacy MXC files. Build cleanup uses built-in Windows PowerShell instead of requiring PowerShell 7.

Main through `a259c566` is integrated, including [#1732](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1732) (fix: prevent intermittent credential reads and false handshake timeouts). Its Connection fixes and surviving release-gated TestHost helpers are preserved; obsolete legacy-executor tests are not restored.

## Evidence

**Current maintainer-validated head: `7d544445fe3cd5f1b671928b429ebbfe1b815780`. Normal ARM64 build and required managed suites passed with GitVersion enabled.**

- Shared: **4,396 passed, 25 opt-in skips, zero failed**. Tray: **4,149 passed, zero skips/failures**. WinNode CLI: **129 passed**. Focused Connection: **57 passed**. Cleanup contracts: **31 passed**.
- The actual host-process pipe fixture ran 30 repetitions. Every owned child exited during cleanup; the maximum measured post-root-exit completion was **612 ms**, within the unchanged three-second assertion.
- New managed regressions cover multiline argv round trips, real approval-coordinator routing, embedded cmd rejection, healthy capacity saturation and immutable cleanup-root protection. Fake SDK and injected unsupported-Windows tests are not native containment proof.
- Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra independently cleared the substantive repair delta `65f52c6d..b611071f`. Later teardown-only, comment-only and main-integration changes were directly inspected. This does not imply an independent full final-head review or clear runtime gates.
- User-approved native-only SDK1 proof: **6 passed, 1 failed, zero skipped**. BaseContainer admission, native protected-path denies without host ACL augmentation, PowerShell startup, output/deadlines, synthetic folder policy and descendant cleanup worked. The TEMP rename assertion failed.
- [Hosted CI run 38988623659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/38988623659), attempt 2: **passed, including CI Gate**, on unchanged merge source. Tray UI: **471 passed, 25 skipped**; Functional UI: **19 passed**; Accessibility: **23 passed**, with zero failures. Attempt 1 aborted at the five-minute inactivity limit after the pre-bootstrap trace, with zero completed UI tests. One failed-jobs retry succeeded; no source change was made for that hang and its exact cause is not established.

**User-directed hold until patched-Windows proof is available.** Native TEMP compatibility fails despite green CI. Strict current-head Gateway/MXC, complete visible UI, signed upgrade and enforcing-SAC proof remain unverified. No TEMP workaround, proof waiver or 90% take-confidence claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Historical author evidence, not current-head maintainer proof</summary>

The author reported normal build, Shared 4,275 passed/25 gated skips, Tray 4,059 passed, five focused cases, exact legacy cleanup fixtures without PowerShell 7, diagram consistency and strict Gateway/MXC 18/18 without skips for source committed as `80d7b368`. The underlying local `review-fixes-validation` bundle was not retrievable in this maintainer session. These reports are retained as historical author claims, not independently verified or current-head runtime evidence.

The author also disclosed a native TEMP rename failure at ancestor `06399086...`, associated with [microsoft/mxc#1204](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1204). The two historical allowlist cases tolerated a child-spawn limitation and establish approval decisions, not universal executable compatibility. None of these gaps is waived.
</details>

Its copied `.git` and GitVersion mutex are independent of other worktrees. No version bypass was used for the following results.

For the managed suites, all three tray data-root overrides used owned temporary directories; `OPENCLAW_TRAY_LOCAL_DATA_DIR` and all native/E2E opt-ins were unset. Fresh test projects were built normally with `dotnet build <project> --verbosity minimal` before the required `--no-restore` runs. Earlier diagnostic runs in the original shared worktree exposed fixture-readiness and deferred-chat-card timing failures. Both cases passed isolated diagnostics and then the full normal suites above. Failure records remain retained; shared-host contention is plausible but not established as their root cause. The measured post-root-exit assertion was not widened.

Local evidence includes the normal build log, five managed TRX files, native TRX/JSON records, process-ownership evidence and an 840-file binary hash manifest. Manifest SHA256: `165DEF80A352FA7BB21CFC022BAB52A60520EBAEA0268976304322D24389E09B`. All frozen binary hashes were unchanged after native proof. Ordinary managed tests and one explicitly approved, bounded native-only run used synthetic roots. SDK probe selected BaseContainer with `NeedsDaclAugmentation=false` and native deny-path support.

- Exact steps or command run: the normal Shared command above executed the real child-process fixture with stdout, stderr and both inherited streams, ten repetitions each. Readiness was gated before releasing the root; completion was measured after its verified exit while the child remained alive.

```json
{"Iterations":30,"AllOwnedChildrenExited":true,"MaxPostRootExitMs":612}
```

- Observed result: the host compatibility executor completed without waiting for descendant pipe EOF, retained short output and cleaned each PID/start-time-verified child. The unsupported-Windows verdict was injected for this test; this is not proof on an actually unsupported OS, native MXC, MCP, or Gateway-mediated execution.

The six passing tests cover default PowerShell startup, stdout/stderr with nonzero exit, synthetic user-folder/protected-path policy, background-descendant cleanup after normal root exit, deadline output retention and default environment isolation. A trailing echo made the command exit zero, but the content assertion correctly failed the test. The upstream [maintainer response](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1204#issuecomment-5769111754) says the fix is in an end-of-October OS update; that fix is not verified on this host.

- Not verified or blocked: passing native TEMP compatibility; strict `.\scripts\validate-mxc-e2e.ps1` without `-AllowSkip`; broad child-executable compatibility; current-head local MCP discovery/invocation; real Gateway path; visible UI; actual unsupported Windows and x64; signed install/upgrade/SAC; packaged private-state behavior; native Gateway lifecycle and complete setup/recovery. The one native-only grant is complete. It did not authorize tray/UI, WSL/Gateway, OS/package installation or SAC changes.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes. Configurable per-folder No access/RO/RW and fixed Windows UI API compatibility change policy behavior.
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No authentication/storage redesign in this migration. Immutable filesystem protection includes credentials, registered Companion state and host-executed `.openclaw-companion` cleanup state. Main's independent credential-read fixes are preserved.
- New or changed network calls? (`Yes`/`No`): No new service endpoint. Network policy remains configurable for contained execution; unsupported-Windows host execution does not enforce it.
- Command or tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes. SDK execution replaces the executable bridge. Approved argv, execution lifetime, bounded output and the positive-unsupported compatibility route are explicit.
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes. Presets use the current-user profile and OS-resolved personal folders, with editable overrides and immutable sensitive-root exclusions.
- If any answer is `Yes`, explain the risk and mitigation: Win32k blocking is intentionally retired for ordinary Windows command compatibility. Contained execution retains desktop isolation, desktop/system-control restrictions, input-injection denial and clipboard/network/filesystem policy. Protected paths reject explicit descendant grants, including prospective cleanup state. No host DACL mutation, whole-drive grant or failure-triggered uncontained downgrade is introduced. The host exception requires positive unsupported-Windows evidence and a persistent warning; approvals still apply. Prelaunch denials and capacity errors do not claim applied containment.

## Compatibility and Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`/`No`): No, not in every policy detail. The Windows UI API restriction, old sandbox Off control and JSON-only `SystemRunBlockHostFallbackWhenMxcUnavailable` setting are retired. Their previous refusal behavior is not retained on positively unsupported Windows.
- Config or environment changes? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes. Retired fields are ignored and omitted on save; `NoAccess=3` preserves legacy `Blocked=2`. Invalid scratch roots fail before filesystem mutation. Build cleanup uses built-in Windows PowerShell; there is no permanent PATH or execution-policy change.
- Migration needed? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes, handled by application/update paths; no manual credential migration is required.
- If yes, list the exact upgrade steps: install/update normally. Exact-file cleanup removes only retired `tools\mxc\{x64,arm64}\wxc-exec.exe` and `wslcsdk.dll` payloads, preserving app-root SDK files, unknown files and user state. Existing folder customizations are preserved; onboarding initializes untouched policy once. Review retained conflicting grants. On unsupported Windows, disable **Run system tools** if uncontained node execution is unacceptable; Gateway-owned `exec` is a separate boundary. Downgrade behavior with No access has not been broadly validated.
